events.title: Early Inhabitants
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human habitation in Cambodia since Neolithic era. Multiple prehistoric sites and pottery discovered.

events.title: Funan Kingdom Founded
events.description: The Khmer people established the Funan Kingdom in the Mekong Delta region, one of Southeast Asia's earliest Indianized states. Funan became a maritime trade center, connecting India and China.

events.title: Funan Prosperity
events.description: The Funan Kingdom controlled the Mekong River basin and parts of the Malay Peninsula, becoming a Southeast Asian power. Chinese historical records documented Funan's tributary relations with China.

events.title: Rise of Chenla
events.description: Chenla (Khmer) separated from Funan and became independent, gradually strengthening. Chenla was precursor to Khmer nation-state.

events.title: Chenla Division
events.description: Chenla split into Land Chenla (north) and Water Chenla (south). This period was politically chaotic with multiple small kingdoms coexisting.

events.title: Angkor Dynasty (Khmer Empire) Founded
events.description: Jayavarman II unified Chenla and established the Angkor Dynasty (Khmer Empire). He proclaimed himself 'Universal Monarch' (God-King), establishing the devaraja cult. The Angkor Dynasty ruled Cambodia for 600 years.

events.title: Yasovarman I Establishes Angkor Capital
events.description: Yasovarman I established capital in Angkor region, beginning Angkor's history as political and religious center.

events.title: Suryavarman II and Construction of Angkor Wat
events.description: During Suryavarman II's reign, the world's largest religious structure, Angkor Wat, was built, dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu. Angkor Wat became a symbol of Khmer culture.

events.title: Cambodian Independence
events.description: Following Sihanouk's independence campaign, Cambodia gained independence from France. November 9 became Cambodia's Independence Day.

events.title: Khmer Rouge Captures Phnom Penh
events.description: The Khmer Rouge, led by Pol Pot, captured Phnom Penh, and the Lon Nol government collapsed. The Khmer Rouge established 'Democratic Kampuchea,' beginning extreme rule.

events.title: Theravada Buddhism Introduced
events.description: Theravada Buddhism from Sri Lanka spread to Cambodia, gradually replacing Hinduism and Mahayana Buddhism, becoming Cambodia's main religion to this day.

events.title: Khmer Rouge Genocide
events.description: Pol Pot implemented extreme communism, forcibly relocating urban populations to rural areas for labor. Intellectuals, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Buddhist monks were massacred in large numbers. About 1.7-2 million people (1/4 of the population) died from execution, starvation, and overwork. This was one of the 20th century's most brutal genocides.

events.title: Constitutional Monarchy Restored
events.description: Elections were held under UN supervision, and Sihanouk became king again. Cambodia restored constitutional monarchy and the kingdom's name.

events.title: French Explorer Discovers Angkor Wat
events.description: French naturalist Henri Mouhot 'discovered' Angkor Wat, introducing this magnificent monument to Western world. This sparked global interest in Khmer civilization.

events.title: French Protectorate
events.description: King Norodom signed treaty making Cambodia French protectorate. France gained control over Cambodia's foreign affairs and gradually expanded control.

events.title: Power Transfer
events.description: Hun Sen's son, Hun Manet, took over as Prime Minister, beginning a family power transfer. Hun Sen became Senate President, retaining actual influence.

events.title: Funan Kingdom
events.description: Funan, one of Southeast Asia's earliest kingdoms, flourished in present-day Cambodia and southern Vietnam. Funan controlled maritime trade routes, maintaining contact with India and China.

events.title: Chenla Kingdom
events.description: Chenla replaced Funan as the region's dominant power. Later Chenla split into Land Chenla (upper Cambodia) and Water Chenla (lower Cambodia).

events.title: Jayavarman VII and Angkor Thom
events.description: Jayavarman VII built Angkor Thom and the Bayon temple, converting the empire to Mahayana Buddhism. His reign marked the Khmer Empire's last great period.

events.title: Independence Movement
events.description: Led by King Sihanouk, Cambodia launched independence movement. Sihanouk used diplomatic and popular mobilization to pressure France. November 9, 1953 became Independence Day.

events.title: Sihanouk Era
events.description: Sihanouk abdicated to become Prime Minister (later Head of State), ruling Cambodia. This was Cambodia's relatively stable and prosperous golden age. Sihanouk pursued neutral foreign policy.

events.title: Lon Nol Coup
events.description: While Sihanouk was abroad, General Lon Nol staged coup, establishing Khmer Republic. Cambodia plunged into civil war. Sihanouk allied with Khmer Rouge to resist Lon Nol.

events.title: Civil War and US Bombing
events.description: Cambodia caught in Vietnam War. US secretly and massively bombed Cambodia, dropping more bombs than all of WWII, killing hundreds of thousands. Khmer Rouge exploited chaos to expand.

events.title: Fall of Angkor
events.description: Siamese forces captured Angkor, forcing the Khmer court to abandon the city. Cambodia's capital moved to Phnom Penh, marking the Angkor era's end.

events.title: Dark Ages
events.description: Cambodia entered decline, repeatedly invaded by Siam and Vietnam. Cambodia became a vassal state caught between two powerful neighbors.

events.title: Sihanouk Becomes King
events.description: 18-year-old Norodom Sihanouk crowned king. France thought him easy to control, but Sihanouk became father of Cambodian independence.

events.title: Vietnamese Withdrawal
events.description: Vietnam withdrew troops from Cambodia after 10-year occupation. UN intervened to mediate peace. Country renamed Kingdom of Cambodia, Buddhism restored as state religion.

events.title: Paris Peace Accords
events.description: All Cambodian factions signed Paris Peace Accords, ending civil war. UN sent peacekeeping force (UNTAC) to oversee transition. Sihanouk returned as king.

events.title: First Democratic Elections
events.description: Cambodia held first democratic elections under UN supervision. New constitution established constitutional monarchy. But political instability continued, Hun Sen gradually consolidated power.

events.title: Coup and Hun Sen Seizes Power
events.description: Hun Sen staged violent coup, ousting co-Prime Minister Ranariddh. Hun Sen became sole Prime Minister, establishing authoritarian rule that continues today.

events.title: Pol Pot's Death and End of Khmer Rouge
events.description: Pol Pot died (possibly murdered), Khmer Rouge remnants surrendered. Cambodia's decades-long nightmare finally ended. But Khmer Rouge tribunal process was slow and incomplete.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: Japan occupied French Indochina including Cambodia. This weakened French colonial rule and sparked Cambodian nationalism.

events.title: Sihanouk Abdication and Sangkum Era
events.description: Sihanouk abdicated to enter politics directly, founding Sangkum Reastr Niyum (People's Socialist Community) party. As prime minister, he pursued neutralism and modernization.

events.title: Vietnam War Spillover
events.description: US secretly bombed Cambodian territory, targeting Vietnamese communist bases. This destabilized Cambodia and radicalized the Khmer Rouge.

events.title: Lon Nol Coup
events.description: General Lon Nol overthrew Sihanouk in US-backed coup. Cambodia renamed Khmer Republic, ending monarchy.

events.title: Cambodian Civil War
events.description: Lon Nol government fought Khmer Rouge. War caused massive casualties; US bombing killed hundreds of thousands of civilians.

events.title: Vietnamese Army Liberates Phnom Penh
events.description: Vietnamese forces captured Phnom Penh, overthrowing Khmer Rouge regime. People's Republic of Kampuchea established, but unrecognized internationally.

events.title: Vietnamese Occupation
events.description: Vietnam occupied Cambodia for 10 years. Though ending Khmer Rouge genocide, this sparked international controversy and guerrilla warfare.

events.title: Paris Peace Accords
events.description: Various Cambodian factions signed Paris Peace Agreements, ending civil war. UN transitional authority established to organize elections.

events.title: Hun Sen Coup
events.description: Hun Sen launched coup against co-Prime Minister Ranariddh, consolidating sole power. Cambodia's fragile democracy severely damaged.

events.title: Pol Pot's Death
events.description: Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot died in jungle, escaping trial. This effectively ended the Khmer Rouge movement.

events.title: Sihanouk Abdication
events.description: King Norodom Sihanouk abdicated due to health. His son Norodom Sihamoni became king. Sihanouk remained 'King-Father' until death in 2012.

events.title: Khmer Rouge Tribunal
events.description: UN-backed Khmer Rouge tribunal began trying surviving leaders. Several top officials convicted of crimes against humanity.

events.title: Hun Sen's Long Rule
events.description: Hun Sen ruled Cambodia for over 38 years, becoming one of world's longest-serving leaders. His rule characterized by authoritarianism, corruption, but also economic growth.

events.title: Chinese Investment Boom
events.description: China became Cambodia's largest investor and aid provider. Massive Chinese investment transformed Cambodian economy but raised debt and sovereignty concerns.

events.title: Sihanouk's Death
events.description: Former King Norodom Sihanouk died in Beijing at 89. Sihanouk was towering figure in modern Cambodian history, dominating politics for 70 years.

events.title: Opposition Gains Strength
events.description: Opposition Cambodia National Rescue Party nearly won elections, challenging CPP's monopoly. This sparked political crisis and Hun Sen's suppression.

events.title: Opposition Party Dissolved
events.description: Hun Sen's government dissolved main opposition party, arrested leader Kem Sokha. This eliminated electoral competition.

events.title: Authoritarian Consolidation
events.description: Hun Sen further consolidated authoritarian rule, controlling media, crushing dissent. Cambodia became one-party state in all but name.

events.title: Economic Challenges
events.description: Despite growth, Cambodia faces poverty, inequality, corruption. Garment industry and tourism are economic pillars, but diversification limited.

events.title: Hun Manet Era Begins
events.description: Hun Manet, Western-educated, faces challenges of continuing father's policies while addressing youth demands and international criticism.

events.title: 權力交接
events.description: 洪森之子洪瑪內接任首相，開始家族權力交接。洪森轉任參議院議長，仍保留實際影響力。...
